[discrete#release-9-2-8.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.2.8 released

[.changelog-source]
__2026-11-09, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.2.8-RELEASE[9.2.8-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.2.8-RELEASE" docker="9.2.8" mini=true %}+++

- **Chat**: link previews, clickable urls in all rich texts
- **CVE-Radar**: findings per node and library, fewer false positives with Debian/Ubuntu advisories, Dependency-Track connection, own backup dump
- **New logo**: web interface, website, app icon
- **App**: changelog, last used tab, wide-screen menu
- **Security**: shorter CSRF token lifetime, library updates (freemarker, jsoup)
- **Docker**: image on Ubuntu 24.04, compose example on PostgreSQL 17

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **Chat and rich texts:** a link in a message shows a preview of the linked page (fetched by the server, removable, can be switched off by administrators); urls in chat messages and all rich texts are clickable, an edited link leads to the edited url; opening a conversation puts the cursor into the message field (not on touch devices).
- **CVE-Radar:** the dialog of an area, system, instance or component lists its open findings with key figures by severity, also per library with the update fixing its CVEs, filterable by the uploaded file they were found in, and can check them again by hand; packages of Debian and Ubuntu are matched against the advisories of their release and by their source package (backported fixes no longer show, also for dpkg-query lists with /etc/os-release), CPE entries of another platform or, by name, of another vendor no longer meet a library, advisories for other operating systems only no longer meet a Linux component; uploading libraries runs in the background; the answers of a team check show their counts and can be filtered; optional connection to Dependency-Track (for now the connection is tested); the imported vulnerability data goes into a dump of its own (adapt an existing backup script, see adminguide).
- **New ProjectForge logo:** in the web interface (light and dark theme), on the website, as favicon and home screen icon, on the Wallet pass of the business card and as app icon.
- **Changelog:** a table of contents of the major versions and their releases beside the text, as on the website (on narrow screens and in the app behind a button); the entry in view is highlighted, the column can be hidden.
- **Lists:** the empty filters business unit, customer and project are shown as one pill in the lists of orders, invoices, projects, cost units and time sheets and in the order statistics.
- **Mobile app (in preparation):** the changelog opens from the "more" menu, the app starts with the tab used last, the menu of the pages has several columns on wide screens and searches while typing, the navigation in landscape can be placed at the right side, the server switch and the settings slide up over the tabs, the daily progress of the time sheets follows the own weekly working hours.
- **Docker:** the image is based on Ubuntu 24.04 and installs the security updates of the base image when it is built; the compose example uses PostgreSQL 17 instead of 13 (an existing database has to be dumped and restored, see docker/README.adoc).
- **Security:** the CSRF token of a session is renewed after an hour at the latest, the task tree and the data transfer box choice change by POST only, requests with a foreign Origin or Referer are refused; security updates of freemarker (2.3.35) and jsoup (1.23.2).
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- [changelog-app]##App## The changelog opens from the "more" menu (the entry with the version).
- [changelog-app]##App## On a wide screen (landscape, iPad) the menu of the pages shows its entries in several columns.
- [changelog-app]##App## In the settings, the navigation in landscape (the column of icons) can be placed at the right side instead of the left, e.g. for the right thumb.
- Chat: a link in a message shows a preview of the linked page (title, description, image), as in other chats, already while writing. The server fetches it, so the browser loads nothing from the linked site; the author can remove the preview (before or after sending), administrators can switch the previews off (projectforge.chat.linkPreview.enabled=false).
- CVE-Radar: optional connection to Dependency-Track, as a second detection of the findings in parallel to the own matching; for now the connection is tested and shown on the system dashboard.
- CVE-Radar: the dialog of an area, system, instance or component has a tab "Findings" with its open findings (key figures of the CVEs by severity, also as filters, counts, filter by certainty, a click opens the CVE); a click on the counts of the tree opens it directly, hovering over them shows the key figures, and the export of the findings stays visible on every row with findings.
- CVE-Radar: the answers of the members to a team check show their counts (answered, not answered yet, affected, per answer) and can be filtered by answer with pinned pills.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- Security: the CSRF token of a session is renewed after an hour at the latest; the task tree and the choice of a personal data transfer box are only changed by POST requests; for browsers without fetch metadata, requests whose Origin or Referer names a foreign host are refused.
- The lists of orders, invoices, projects, cost units and time sheets and the order statistics show the empty filters business unit, customer and project as one pill; a filter gets its own pill once something is selected in it.
- Chat messages and all rich texts (descriptions, notes, alerts) show their urls (with http(s):// or www.) as clickable links, also older texts and a url typed as the last word.
- Changelog: a table of contents of the major versions and their releases beside the text (on narrow screens and in the app behind a button), as on the website; the entry in view is highlighted and the column can be hidden.
- Chat: opening a conversation puts the cursor into the message field (not on touch devices, where the keyboard would cover the messages).
- **CVE-Radar**
  * Packages of Debian and Ubuntu (SBOMs of containers and servers) are matched against the advisories of their release from OSV.dev: fixes backported by the distribution no longer show as possibly affected, open CVEs of the release as affected, CVEs without impact (unimportant, negligible) not at all. New OSV ecosystems Debian and Ubuntu, on by default.
  * Binary packages of a distribution (libssl3) are matched by their source package (openssl), as the advisories name it (upstream qualifier of an SBOM). A dpkg-query list with the lines of /etc/os-release and the source packages is matched like an SBOM; the command in the user guide writes them.
  * Fewer false positives by the name of a CPE: an entry for a runtime (node.js, Rust, Python, …) only meets libraries of that ecosystem, and for libraries known to OSV the vendor has to fit the package (Adobe Connect is no longer the npm package connect).
- **CVE-Radar**
  * Findings per library: the tab "Findings" switches to one row per library with the number of its CVEs, the highest severity and the update that fixes them at once; the export has the same summary.
  * The findings of a node can be checked again by hand ("Check again" in the dialog of its findings); the message tells how many are new, changed or removed.
  * Every library uploaded for a component shows where it was found: the file of the upload and, in the SBOM of an image, the place inside it.
  * The findings of a node can be filtered by the uploaded file they were found in; the key figures and counts then show that file only.
  * Advisories for other operating systems only (e.g. Windows) no longer match a component running on Linux.
  * Uploading the libraries runs in the background with a progress bar, so a large upload no longer runs into a timeout.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- [changelog-app]##App## The app starts with the tab used last on the device instead of always with the business cards, and the pages tab (globe) with the page shown last.
- [changelog-app]##App## The server switch and the settings of the "more" menu slide up over the tabs like the notifications, the tab bar stays visible below them (adding a server and the log open within them, with an arrow back); the "more" menu grows as high as its entries need.
- [changelog-app]##App## New app icon with the new ProjectForge logo.
- [changelog-app]##App## The progress of a day in the time sheets is measured against a fifth of the own weekly working hours valid on that day instead of 8 hours.
- CVE-Radar: the imported data of the vulnerabilities is stored in a table of its own; the backup script writes it with the OSV advisories and the state of the imports into a dump of its own (projectforge_cveradar_…), restorable from the sources. Cases, team checks, answers and findings stay in the main dump, which is complete without it. Adapt an existing backup script (adminguide, “Backup script”).
- New ProjectForge logo: in the web interface (light and dark theme), on the website, as favicon and icon of the browser and the home screen, and on the Wallet pass of the business card.
- Docker: the image is based on Ubuntu 24.04 (Eclipse Temurin 21 JRE, formerly Ubuntu 22.04) and installs the security updates of the base image when it is built; the compose example uses PostgreSQL 17 instead of 13, which is out of support (an existing database has to be dumped and restored, see docker/README.adoc).

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- [changelog-app]##App## The + of the addresses opens the form of a new address instead of an error page (not found).
- [changelog-app]##App## The search of the pages menu shows its results while typing, above the keyboard (not only after the search key).
- Chat messages and rich texts: a link whose url is edited afterwards leads to the edited url, not to the one typed first.
- Security updates of the libraries freemarker (2.3.35) and jsoup (1.23.2).
====

[discrete#release-9-2-7.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.2.7 released

[.changelog-source]
__2026-11-08, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.2.7-RELEASE[9.2.7-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.2.7-RELEASE" docker="9.2.7" mini=true %}+++

- **CVE-Radar**: EUVD as an additional source, team checks answered per person
- **App**: pushes from all servers, new menu of the ProjectForge tab, browser functions in web tabs
- **Edited by**: new column in many lists
- **E-invoice**: self-check of the generated file, separate contact emails
- **Business cards**: photo linked by a public url with a random token

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **CVE-Radar:** import of the European Union Vulnerability Database (EUVD, off by default) with EUVD id, EPSS and exploitation day; the source (NVD, OSV, EUVD) is shown as a badge and can be filtered; a team check can ask every member of a group and stays open until all active members answered; new notification rule "Unanswered team checks of a case"; statistics can look back 1, 2, 5 or 10 years.
- **Mobile app (in preparation):** pushes of all logged-in servers, the ProjectForge tab opens with a menu (favorites, last pages, main menu, user menu with appearance, search), web tabs have a browser menu, the system message is shown, contacts can be added to the device or shared as vCard, the notifications and the "more" menu slide up over the tab bar, the week strip of the time sheets snaps to whole weeks.
- **Lists:** new column "Edited by" in the lists of address campaign values, invoices, orders, leave corrections, liquidity entries, mail, contracts, the visitor book, notification rules, customers and projects; address campaign values can be filtered by editor.
- **E-invoice:** the generated XRechnung/ZUGFeRD file is checked by the e-invoice checker and the result is shown; the recipient email (BT-49) and the contact email (BT-58) are separate fields, the seller's contact email (BT-43) is prefilled and editable.
- **Digital business cards:** the photo is linked by a public url with a random token, also without a gateway (update the gateway together with the server; photo links of earlier QR codes stop working); the card lists its contents below the QR code, which is rendered sharper.
- **Chat and notifications:** the search lists all matching people with buttons for a direct message or an encrypted chat, a long press on a reaction shows who reacted, chat notifications show the beginning of the message, notification mails contain a link; the rule types of notification rules come from the active modules and plugins.
- **Fixes:** calendar entries can be resized from the start time, a time sheet opened from a break keeps its end time, plugin menu entries can be chosen in notification rules, the badges of the app follow chat reads and done notifications at once.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- CVE-Radar: import of the vulnerabilities of the European Union Vulnerability Database (EUVD) as a supplement to the NVD. It adds the EUVD id, the EPSS and the day of exploitation, and brings vulnerabilities the NVD doesn't have yet, also ones without a CVE id. The EUVD names products only, so these match as possible. Off by default.
- CVE-Radar: the list and the file of a vulnerability show where its data comes from (NVD, OSV, EUVD) as badges, and the list has a pinned filter to select by source.
- [changelog-app]##App## The system message of the administrators (e.g. maintenance work) is shown above the pages, as in the web version.
- Address campaign values: new filter "Edited by" to list the entries a chosen user has created or changed.
- [changelog-app]##App## The web tabs have a browser menu with back, forward, reload, find in the page, share link, open in the browser and restart; pull to refresh now also works on the pages with the menu, and a lost connection shows an error with a retry instead of an empty page.
- New column "Edited by" with a pill for everybody who created or changed an entry, in the lists of address campaign values, outgoing and incoming invoices, orders, leave corrections, liquidity entries, incoming and outgoing mail, contracts, the visitor book, notification rules, customers and projects.
- CVE-Radar, notification rules: new rule type "Unanswered team checks of a case". The rule names a case and reminds the members who haven't answered one of its team checks asking every member yet, at most once a day, by schedule or triggered by hand. The reminder is done as soon as they answered.
- [changelog-app]##App## All servers the app is logged in at send pushes, not only the one shown. The push names its server, a tap on one of another server offers to switch there and opens it; their open notifications are shown at the menu, in the server list and in the notification center, the icon counts all of them. Older servers push only while shown, as before.
- [changelog-app]##App## A contact of the address book can be added to the own contacts of the device or shared as vCard (messages, mail, messengers), also without a connection to the server.
- [changelog-app]##App## The ProjectForge tab (globe) opens with a menu that is easy to reach on a phone: tabs for the favorites, the pages opened last, the main menu with expandable areas and the user menu with the appearance (light, dark, system; the tab chosen last opens again), and a search across all entries (or in all data). Tapping the globe again closes the menu and shows the page as it was; tapped once more, it opens the menu again.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- CVE-Radar, tab "Statistics": optionally look back 1, 2, 5 or 10 years.
- CVE-Radar, My CVE-Radar: "Done" and "Not affected" ask before saving and explain that they answer for yourself only and don't close the case. The case card also shows the checks of your own groups with their answer button. If such a check asks every member, its answer is your answer to the case as well, so there is only one answer per person. In the table of these checks the identifying columns and the actions stay pinned.
- Chat: on touch devices and in the app, a long press on a reaction shows who reacted.
- Chat: the search lists all matching people, each with buttons to start a direct message or an encrypted chat.
- E-invoice: the customer's invoice recipient email (BT-49) and the email of its contact person (BT-58) are separate fields now, on invoice and account. The seller's contact email (BT-43) is prefilled from the configuration and editable on the invoice.
- [changelog-app]##App## Below the QR code of a business card a small list shows every field the card contains, including the photo, also without a connection to the server.
- Digital business card: below the QR code a small list shows every field the card contains, including the photo.
- The QR code of a business card is rendered at a higher resolution, so it stays sharp when shown large (e.g. in the app).

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- Digital business cards: the photo is linked by a public url with a random token (no login, not guessable), also without a gateway; the url stays the same when the image is replaced or deleted, and can be revoked with "Renew photo link" on the card. The base url can be set with `+projectforge.businessCard.photoBaseUrl+`. Update the gateway together with the server; photo links of earlier QR codes stop working.
- Creating an e-invoice (XRechnung, ZUGFeRD) now runs the e-invoice checker over the generated file and shows the result (valid, warnings or errors) in a dialog.
- Notification rules: the rule types come from the modules and plugins that provide them. The rule types of a deactivated plugin (e.g. the CVE-Radar) aren't offered any more, and its rules wait until the plugin is active again.
- [changelog-app]##App## The week strip of the time sheets follows the finger when swiped and snaps to a whole week; the week starts on the first day of the week set in "My account".
- The notifications of chat messages show the beginning of the message (in rooms with its author) instead of repeating their title, in the app and in the notification center of the web pages. Only for the recipient while they may read the conversation; mails and pushes keep their generic text.
- [changelog-app]##App## The notifications (bell) and the "more" menu slide up over the tabs like the menu of the pages, the tab bar stays visible below them; pulling them down, a tap above them or their button again closes them.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- CVE-Radar: a team check can ask every member of the group (e.g. everyone checks the own client); each answer is stored and the check stays open until all members answered who logged in within the last 90 days (configurable). Before, every answer replaced the one before.
- Calendar: the start time of an entry can now be changed by dragging its top edge, not only the end time.
- Notification mails (e.g. about new chat messages) now contain a link to the chat or the concerned entry.
- Notification rules: the menu entries of plugins (e.g. the CVE-Radar) can be chosen as menu counter and as link of the notifications.
- [changelog-app]##App## The badges of the chat and the notifications follow at once: a push sets the bell's count when it arrives, and a chat read or a notification done in the pages removes them right away, no longer only with the next update a minute later.
- Calendar: a time sheet opened from a break keeps its end time when the start time is changed.
====

[discrete#release-9-2-5.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.2.5: report and block in the chat, CVE-Radar with OSV.dev, configurable password rules

[.changelog-source]
__2026-11-03, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.2.5-RELEASE[9.2.5-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.2.5-RELEASE" docker="9.2.5" mini=true %}+++

- **Chat**: report messages, block users
- **CVE-Radar**: libraries matched against the advisories of OSV.dev
- **Passwords**: configurable number of character classes
- Fix: the gross sum of an invoice matches the e-invoice to the cent

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **Chat:** messages of others can be reported to the administrators, and users can be blocked: no direct messages, notifications, mentions or search hits of them.
- **CVE-Radar:** the libraries of the inventory are matched by package and version against the advisories of OSV.dev (Maven, npm, PyPI, NuGet, Packagist, Go, crates.io), also when the NVD names them late or not at all.
- **Login:** the number of character classes a password must contain (e.g. 3 of 4) is configurable next to the minimum length; login names in projectforge.2fa.exemptUsers need no second factor, e.g. the account of an app store review.
- **Mobile app (in preparation):** the chat tab shows no menu of the web version, tapping the chat button again leads back to the chat start page; sharper address images in the address list.
- **Fixes:** the gross sum of an invoice is the net sum plus the vat sum and no longer differs by a cent from the e-invoice; the e-invoice export refuses sums that differ from the invoice; the invoice document shows quantity and unit price with all their decimals.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- Setting projectforge.2fa.exemptUsers: login names that need no second factor, e.g. for the account of an app store review.
- Chat: messages of others can be reported to the administrators, and users can be blocked (no direct messages, no notifications, mentions or search hits of them).
- CVE-Radar: the libraries of the inventory are matched by package and version against the advisories of OSV.dev (Maven, npm, PyPI, NuGet, Packagist, Go, crates.io), also when the NVD names them late or not at all; a matching advisory becomes a vulnerability whatever its score.
- Passwords: the number of character classes a password must contain (uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, special characters, e.g. 3 of 4) is configurable next to the minimum length.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- Address images: larger preview images, so they look sharp in the app's address list (existing previews are renewed when the images are shrunk again in the administration).
- [changelog-app]##App## The chat tab shows no menu of the web version; tapping the chat button again leads back to the chat start page.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- **Invoices: the invoice document and the e-invoice use the same formulas**
  * The gross sum is the net sum plus the vat sum. It was the sum of the positions' gross amounts, whose vat is rounded per position, and could differ by a cent from the e-invoice, so the recipient could reject the invoice.
  * The export of an e-invoice (XRechnung, ZUGFeRD) compares its sums with those of the invoice and refuses the export if they differ.
  * The invoice document shows quantity and unit price with all their decimals, as the e-invoice does, instead of rounded to two.
====

[discrete#release-9-2-4.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.2.4: e-invoice buyer fields, mobile app with several servers and task tree, daily error digest

[.changelog-source]
__2026-11-02, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.2.4-RELEASE[9.2.4-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.2.4-RELEASE" docker="9.2.4" mini=true %}+++

- **E-invoice**: order number, department and cost center of the buyer
- **Mobile app** (in preparation): switch between several servers, task tree for time sheets
- App and server warn each other if the other side is too old
- **Error digest** once a day instead of every hour
- Fix: connecting the app behind an SSO proxy works at the first attempt

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **E-invoice:** new fields order number (BT-13), department of the orderer (BT-56) and cost center (BT-19) on the invoice and the account; the form labels name the e-invoice term (BT-x); the invoice template gets the variables Bestellnummer and Kostenstelle, the department is part of the address.
- **Mobile app (in preparation):** the logins of several servers are kept and the server can be switched in the account menu; time sheets choose the structure element in the task tree, with a search over the whole path, and cost units in a scrollable selection box; a warning if the app is too old for the server or the server too old for the app, "My account" marks outdated apps.
- **Error digest:** sent once a day at 07:00, only urgent problems send it early (at most once an hour); configurable.
- **Order mails:** clearer layout with the buttons at the top and a button to the order notification settings.
- **Fixes:** connecting the app behind an SSO proxy works at the first attempt, also when the proxy returns the browser without the parameters of the link.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- [changelog-app]##App## A warning if the app is too old for the server or the server too old for the app; "My account" marks outdated apps.
- [changelog-app]##App## The logins of several servers are kept, and the server can be switched in the account menu without logging in again; another server is added there too.
- E-invoice: new fields order number (BT-13), department of the orderer (BT-56) and cost center (BT-19) on the invoice and the account (department, cost center); the labels of the invoice and account forms name the e-invoice term (BT-x) the field is sent in. The invoice template gets the variables Bestellnummer and Kostenstelle (with isBestellnummer/isKostenstelle), the department is part of the address.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- [changelog-app]##App## Time sheets: the structure element can be chosen in the task tree (level by level, starting at the current one, with a search in the level and everything below it), the search finds words of the whole path, the path is shown above the title, cost units are chosen in a scrollable selection box with number and text, the time sheet tab is no longer marked as under construction, and the templates open in a list instead of a row of chips.
- Order mails: clearer layout with the buttons at the top, and a button to the order notification settings.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- Error digest: the regular digest is sent once a day at 07:00 instead of every hour, only urgent problems (security, data, immediate events) send it early, at most once an hour. Configurable by projectforge.support.errorDigest.interval, sendAt and urgentMinGap.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- [changelog-app]##App## Connecting the app behind an SSO proxy works at the first attempt, also when the proxy brings the browser back from its login without the parameters of the link.
====

====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- **Mobile app: notifications and push (iPhone)**
  * [changelog-app]##App## The notifications of the web version (rules, chat) are shown in the app as well: a bell with the count, the list with the archive, and confirming or finishing them; a link opens the page in the app.
  * [changelog-app]##App## A new notification wakes the app with a push message (APNs, `+projectforge.push.apns.*+`), without its content in the message. Without a configured key nothing is sent and the app polls as before.
- **Mobile app (in preparation): time sheets**
  * [changelog-app]##App## The app books time sheets on the phone: a week strip with the daily totals, the bookings of the day with the gaps between them (a tap books a gap), recent bookings and templates to start from, a task search, and the cost unit chosen automatically where the task has only one. The server's checks (overlap, closed tasks, protected periods) apply as in the web version.
  * [changelog-app]##App## A timer in the app starts and stops a booking on the device; stopping opens the form with the time rounded to 5 minutes.
  * [changelog-app]##App## The time sheet list of the web pages switches to the app's tab; the form of a single booking stays in the web pages when opened from a link.
- **CVE-Radar: notification without details and about outdated lists of libraries**
  * A new notification rule "New findings of the CVE radar" starts with a text that names no details ("there may be updates") and a link to the list; the new variable cvrListLink always links to the list.
  * New rule type "Outdated lists of libraries of the CVE radar": the responsible team of a component whose list of libraries was applied more than a number of days ago (30 by default) is told, at most once a week, and the notification is resolved by an update of the list. The day of the last list is now recorded per component.
- **Mobile app (in preparation)**
  * [changelog-app]##App## Behind an SSO proxy (e.g. Authentik as forward auth) the app gets the proxy's session from the browser login (`+projectforge.app.proxyCookies+`); when it expires, the app logs in again in the browser.
  * [changelog-app]##App## The login of the app offers the recently used servers, and the logout works even if the server can't be reached.
  * [changelog-app]##App## Business cards are stored in the app and shown offline too; they are reloaded silently when the tab is opened and by a button, and can be added to the Apple Wallet if the server is configured for it (iPhone), also by the link of the web page in the app.
  * [changelog-app]##App## The app gives more room to the pages: no title bar above the web pages and the chat, a slim navigation bar with icons only, and in landscape a narrow navigation at the side.
  * [changelog-app]##App## In the app, the menu entries "Chat" and "My business cards" and the bell of the web pages switch to the app's own tab; the new settings of the app can keep each of them in the web version.
  * [changelog-app]##App## The app has an address book like the Contacts app: a search field, sections with an index at the side, and tapping a number offers a call or a message, a mail address opens the mail app. All addresses are stored on the device (also offline) and updated silently; editing opens the form of the web pages, and the address list of the web pages switches to the app's tab.
  * [changelog-app]##App## The app's own screens follow the light or dark appearance chosen in the web pages (also offline), and the web pages no longer flash white while loading.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- Faster first page of big lists: the CVE-Radar start page no longer loads every vulnerability to build the list

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- Calendar on small screens: the calendar chooser has a line of its own under the title and the buttons instead of being covered by them.
- **CVE-Radar: the file of an incident opens again and has a tab for its description**
  * The file of a case without a CVE showed an empty page. It now opens on the new first tab "Description", which shows the description of the case and lets the security team edit it with a rich text editor.
- Kost2 sometimes missing in overviews such as the structure tree, the project list or the cost unit selection of a time sheet, although it existed: for instance after a project was reactivated, or for a cost unit created while the caches were being reloaded in the background.
- Order book: a payment schedule dated in a following month now also defers the invoice of a finished position (filter "to be invoiced", next invoice date)
====

[discrete#release-9-2-1.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.2.1: CVE-Radar with AI prompts and ad-hoc check, Apple Wallet, mobile layout

[.changelog-source]
__2026-11-01, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.2.1-RELEASE[9.2.1-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.2.1-RELEASE" docker="9.2.1" mini=true %}+++

- **CVE-Radar**: ad-hoc check of uploaded files, findings report and case research with prompts for an approved AI system
- **Digital business cards** in the Apple Wallet
- More room for content on **mobile devices**
- Fix: planned invoices no longer count in the invoice statistics

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **CVE-Radar:** ad-hoc check of lockfiles, SBOMs or a zip of such lists against all vulnerabilities without storing anything; export of the open findings of a project with a prompt for advice on the fix; research of a new case with an AI system; download and import of a case as JSON; upload of all lists of a component in one zip and the lockfile of pnpm.
- **Digital business cards:** add a card to the Apple Wallet (needs a Pass Type ID certificate).
- **Mobile app (in preparation):** login via the browser with second factor, the own business cards also without network, connected apps listed in My account.
- **Mobile devices:** on narrow or low screens the logo row and the status bar are hidden, smaller paddings, a compact list footer, scrollable tabs; very low screens scroll.
- **Fixes:** planned invoices no longer count in the statistics of the invoice list.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- Digital business cards: add a card to the Apple Wallet (needs a Pass Type ID certificate, see the admin guide).
- **CVE-Radar: ad-hoc check of uploaded files against all vulnerabilities**
  * The new page Ad-hoc check takes lockfiles, SBOMs, build tool output or a zip with such lists and checks every package against the imported vulnerabilities, with a progress bar per file. Nothing is stored; every reader may check, and only the person who started a check sees its result.
  * The result lists the vulnerabilities with package, version, file and the case of the security team, can be downloaded as JSON, and comes with a prompt asking an approved AI system how to fix them. The names of the files are replaced by default.
- **CVE-Radar: research a new case with an AI system**
  * Research with AI (security team) builds a prompt for an approved AI system from the CVE id or a description of the incident, sources and notes, with the NVD data of an imported CVE. There is no direct connection: the prompt is copied there, its answer pasted back. The dialog has three steps (details, prompt, answer), each with the way back; the prompt can be copied or downloaded as a file.
  * The answer (one JSON block) is checked and shown as a preview with a copy button per value; Create case creates the case with title, description, priority and reason, fix version, workaround, measures and references, marked as created with the help of an AI system.
- **CVE-Radar: download a case as JSON and import it again**
  * Download as JSON in the file of a case saves its values as stored (without status, assignee, ratings, team checks and discussion).
  * Import case (security team) creates a new case from such a file after a preview, e.g. to copy a case into another instance of ProjectForge.
  * Import case also takes the answer of an AI system to the prompt of Research with AI, e.g. saved as a file; quotes made typographic by copying are straightened.
- **CVE-Radar: export the findings of a project, with a prompt for advice on the fix**
  * The open findings of a node of the inventory and below as one JSON file: per vulnerability the NVD data, the case of the security team and the matched technologies with versions and package URLs. Only what the user may see; internal names are replaced by neutral ones by default.
  * A prompt with the report asks an approved AI system how to fix every vulnerability in the project: whether it is really affected, the target version and how to force it for a transitive dependency, a workaround, and how to verify the fix.
- **CVE-Radar: more ways to upload the libraries of a component**
  * All lists of a component can be uploaded in one zip, collected by a script of the project (the user guide has an example): lockfiles, SBOMs, output of the build tools and package lists of the images. Only the files of such lists are read; files that may hold tokens (.npmrc, .env, gradle.properties, settings.xml) are skipped unread. The preview shows every file of the zip with its format.
  * The lockfile of pnpm (pnpm-lock.yaml, versions 5, 6 and 9) is read, without the development dependencies.
  * The upload dialog shows how to list the packages of a container image (e.g. eclipse-temurin: dpkg-query, apk, rpm or an SBOM from syft), where native libraries such as brotli, zlib or OpenSSL show up, and links to the chapter of the user guide.
- **Mobile app (in preparation)**
  * [changelog-app]##App## The ProjectForge app for iOS and Android logs in via the browser, with password and second factor (WebAuthn or code) as usual; the browser asks once more before an app is connected. The first version shows the own digital business cards, also without network.
  * [changelog-app]##App## All other pages of ProjectForge open inside the app, without a second login. Logging out the app ends them as well.
  * [changelog-app]##App## My account: the connected apps with their last usage, each can be logged out. A password change logs out all apps; an app unused for 90 days is logged out automatically.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- **More room for content on mobile devices**
  * On narrow or low screens (e.g. a phone in landscape) the logo row and the status bar are hidden, and the paddings of edit pages, tabs, action bar and list footer are smaller; changelog, version and copyright are in the user menu there.
  * The list footer shows only the range and the page buttons around the current page; the tabs of an edit page scroll horizontally.
  * The menu of an area at the top right of its pages (e.g. CVE-Radar) is a single menu button on narrow screens; on the file of a CVE-Radar case the header scrolls with the content on narrow or low screens.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- Outgoing invoices: planned invoices no longer count in the statistics of the invoice list (gross, net, open, overdue).
- Small screens: on a very low display (e.g. a phone in landscape) the page now scrolls, so the content below the header is reachable.
====

[discrete#release-9-2-0.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.2: Java 21, JCR removed, CVE-Radar, digital business cards

[.changelog-source]
__2026-10-30, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.2.0-RELEASE[9.2.0-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.2.0-RELEASE" docker="9.2.0" %}+++

[.changelog-checksum]
SHA-256 of projectforge-application-9.2.0.jar: `+3189e644cfef3e1b9d7215147f1617c4b1430b33899ce949608d6d6852303df8+`

- [red]##**Java 21 required**##, **JCR removed** (migrate with 9.1.x first)
- **CVE-Radar** (plugin): NVD import, inventory of systems, matching with notifications, triage
- **Digital business cards** with QR code (vCard)
- Order notifications per user: at once, daily summary or none
- Forecast: new breakdown table; fixes for stale invoice lists and paged list searches

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **Java 21:** required from 9.2 on, the executable JAR no longer starts on Java 17.
- **Files:** the JCR (Apache Oak) is removed, attachments live in the database and data transfer files in the file system.
- **CVE-Radar:** cases and team checks, import of vulnerabilities from the NVD, an inventory of systems with a technology catalogue and library import (SBOM, lockfiles, package lists), matching of vulnerabilities against the inventory with a notification rule for new findings, a file per CVE with ratings, measures and discussion.
- **Digital business cards:** several cards per user with a QR code, data taken over from an address.
- **Order notifications:** per user at once, as a daily summary or not at all; a recipient gets at most one mail and one SMS per rule and day.
- **Forecast and contribution margin:** new table "Breakdown of the forecast", preliminary revenue of unbooked invoices from the cost assignments.
- **Projects:** the status is acquisition, active, paused or ended.
- **Performance and usability:** fewer requests per page view, upload speed in the data transfer, sideways paging of chat images, dialogs ask before discarding input.
- **Fixes:** invoice lists with stale paid status after a mass update, outdated results in long searched lists.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====
[red]##**Java 21 is required**## - ProjectForge 9.2 is compiled for Java 21, the executable JAR no longer starts on Java 17. The Docker image already contains Java 21.

[red]##**JCR removed**## - Files are kept by the file store (attachments in the database, data transfer files in the file system). **If you still use the JCR, migrate with 9.1.x first**, before you update to 9.2. See the admin guide, "Moving the files out of the JCR".

**Before updating** - Back up the database; its schema is migrated automatically at the first start.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- **CVE-Radar (plugin, not active by default): first part with real data**
  * Cases: vulnerabilities and incidents without CVE with measures, fix criteria and a closure overview telling whether a case can be closed.
  * Team checks: groups answer whether their projects or systems are affected.
  * Import of the versions and check results of a client agent from a log server (Graylog), configurable.
  * My CVE-Radar: employees confirm the measures and see their own devices.
- **CVE-Radar: vulnerabilities from the NVD**
  * Import of the vulnerabilities (CVEs) from the National Vulnerability Database on schedule and in the job monitor, incrementally and from a configurable CVSS score on; off by default.
  * The start page of the CVE-Radar lists the imported vulnerabilities with score, severity, weaknesses and dates; the prototype with test data moved to a demo page linked from there.
  * The tab "Statistics" of the CVE-Radar shows the reported cases and the vulnerabilities published by the NVD per day, week or month.
- Data transfer (also public): the upload shows its current speed in kB/s or MB/s.
- **CVE-Radar: inventory of systems**
  * Systems as a tree: areas of any depth, below them systems with instances (installations), components and technologies. Everybody creates areas for a group of their own; the groups of an area and the areas above it see and change what is below, the security team reads internal systems.
  * Areas and systems can be moved; the security officer moves an area below another one, e.g. below a customer.
  * Technology catalogue: ecosystems, products and frameworks, and libraries as a tree (a library may belong to several frameworks). The security team maintains it, the technologies of a component are picked from it.
  * Libraries of a component from lists: SBOMs (CycloneDX or SPDX as JSON, all ecosystems and operating system packages by their package URL), the lockfiles of npm, yarn, Composer, Go, Cargo and the pinned requirements of Python, package lists of Debian, Alpine and RPM systems, the output of Maven or Gradle, or the file names of a jar, several files merged, including the transitive dependencies; a list with a search field shows them. The preview before applying shows what is new, removed or changed in its version. The dialog shows which file or command to take.
- **CVE-Radar: file of a CVE with ratings, measures and discussion**
  * A row of the vulnerability list opens the file of the CVE: NVD data with the remediation hints apart from the other references, the ratings of the security team members side by side, the binding priority with a reason, the measures for techies and non-techies, fix version, workaround and references.
  * Take over, assign, status and a suggested priority from the CVSS score and the CISA KEV catalogue; a change over a newer version of the case is refused.
  * Discussion of a case in the chat for all readers; every team check has a file of its own with a discussion that only the asked group and the security team see.
  * The roles of the CVE-Radar (readers, security team, security officers) are PF groups named in the settings `+readGroup+`, `+writeGroup+` and `+securityOfficerGroup+`.
- **Digital business cards**
  * Several cards per user, each with a QR code (vCard) to show, e.g. as a screenshot. Reached from the user menu and the address list.
  * The data is taken over from an address of the address book (the own one is suggested), picked per field and editable; private data only if ticked.
  * The photo of the own address can be linked in the vCard: the gateway delivers it under a signed url and needs no further data for it.
- Order notifications (a button on the order list and beside the e-mail checkbox of each order): choose per user whether the e-mails about changed orders arrive at once, as one daily summary or not at all, as a default and as exceptions for single projects or customers.
- **CVE-Radar: vulnerabilities matched against the inventory**
  * Every imported vulnerability is matched against the technologies of the inventory, after each import and each change of the inventory or of the catalogue: by the CPE or the catalogue entry of a technology, otherwise by its name (then only "possibly affected"), with the version ranges of the NVD. A component of a system counts for every instance of it.
  * The findings show in the file of a CVE (tab "Affected"), as a count with a filter "With matches in the inventory" in the list of vulnerabilities and in the inventory tree, where affected rows are highlighted. Installations a person may not see are only counted. The security team discards false positives with a reason; a discarded finding stays discarded, even after a version was changed and reverted.
  * The inventory tree shows when the technologies of a component were last updated.
  * Discussions about a CVE take attachments, which are deleted after 30 days; the notice about confidential details shows in orange while writing.
  * New notification rule type "New findings of the CVE radar": the responsible team of an affected system (the group of the system or of the nearest area above) is notified, the recipients of the rule in copy, right after the matching found something new. A rule starts from a CVSS severity (known exploited vulnerabilities always), optionally with possible findings and vulnerabilities not yet rated. Each notification names only the systems visible to its recipient and every finding once; the text has variables for the vulnerabilities, the systems, the highest severity and a link.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- Tables no longer store their unchanged column layout again on every page view.
- Fewer requests per page view: the unread chat count of the top bar comes with the user status instead of two list requests, it is counted once for menu and status, and the event stream stops retrying after the session expired.
- Order statistics, forecast: new table "Breakdown of the forecast" per month with the invoiced sums, the remaining forecast of commissioned fixed price and flat rate positions, of commissioned time & materials positions (run rate) and of not yet commissioned positions (weighted), and the part of the forecast for which an invoice is already planned.
- Chat: the images of a message stand side by side (scrolling sideways when there are many), and the full size view pages through them with buttons and arrow keys.
- Dialogs with input fields ask before they are closed by a click beside them, Esc or the close button once something was entered, so the input is no longer lost by accident.
- Properties editor: the descriptions link to the matching sections of the admin guide and support code, bold text and links.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- Java 21 is required from version 9.2 on: ProjectForge is compiled for Java 21, the executable JAR no longer starts on Java 17. The Docker image already contains Java 21.
- Contribution margin: the preliminary revenue of unbooked outgoing invoices is taken from the cost assignments of the invoice positions (kost2 → project) if they are completely defined; otherwise from the project of the invoice as before.
- Files: the JCR (Apache Oak) is removed, all files are stored by the file store (attachments in the database, data transfer files in the file system). An installation still using the JCR has to migrate with 9.1.x first: ProjectForge refuses to start, if the JCR contains files, which weren't migrated. The JCR backup and the migration were removed from the system page, projectforge.jcr.maxDefaultFileSize is now projectforge.files.maxDefaultFileSize (the old key is still read, with a warning on start until it is renamed; obsolete JCR properties are reported too).
- Projects: the status is one of acquisition, active, paused and ended (or not set). Existing projects were mapped: build phase, productive and maintenance became active, on hold became paused. The history still shows the former values.
- The system configuration page now offers the projectforge.properties editor and the comparison with its backups for administrators, as the System page does.
- User menu: "Customize my menu" comes before "My account".

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- Invoice lists: an invoice that was marked as paid could stay in the filter "unpaid" (and in its sums) after a mass update, even after the caches were refreshed.
- Notification rules: a recipient gets at most one mail and one SMS per rule and day, even if a rule created several notifications. The next day, it reminds again. Tests are not limited.
- Long lists (orders, invoices, time sheets, accounting records, vulnerabilities): a search could show an outdated, e.g. empty, result after changes made at the same time or directly in the database. Reloading the page now always shows the current result.

++++
{% include download-link.html %}
++++
====

[discrete#release-9-1-0.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.1: new file store, chat, more pages migrated, last release with JCR and Java 17

[.changelog-source]
__2026-10-28, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.1.0-RELEASE[9.1.0-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.1.0-RELEASE" docker="9.1.0" %}+++

[.changelog-checksum]
SHA-256 of projectforge-application-9.1.0.jar: `+4a44437a42a8bdfaeaef8ca915d4edd0635b16cd4a5a83bcb53f5854fe31e743+`

- [red]##**Last release with JCR and Java 17**##: migrate the JCR with 9.1.x before updating to 9.2+
- **New file store** in the database replacing the JCR
- **Chat**: rooms, direct messages, confidential conversations, files, avatars, data transfer chats
- **Contribution margin** per order and structure element, **forecast** and **customer wizard**
- **Security hardening**: stricter access checks, CSP, CSRF for every session, `+config.xml+` replaced by configuration parameters
- More pages migrated: users, addresses, vacation, employees, banking, polls, contracts and more

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **JCR and Java 17:** 9.1.x is the last release that supports the JCR and runs on Java 17. Migrate the files with 9.1.x before updating to 9.2 or later, which require Java 21 (the Docker image already is based on it).
- **File store:** with `+projectforge.files.store=db+` all files are stored in the database (schema `+pf_files+`), data transfer files in the file system, compressed and optionally encrypted at rest; the JCR files are copied in the background and verified by size and checksum, with a report. Backups: a main dump plus a dump of the files.
- **Chat:** rooms and direct messages with formatting, files, threads, mentions, quotes, search, avatars, end-to-end encrypted confidential conversations and a chat in every data transfer area.
- **Statistics:** contribution margin per order and structure element with a bubble chart, faster forecast and contribution margin, rearrangeable chart tiles, forecast snapshot date, liquidity forecast with a free number of days.
- **Customers and projects:** customer wizard, projects independent of cost units with configurable number ranges, project contacts instead of fixed roles, project groups, order access of project managers per customer, customer group or business unit, new user right Customers.
- **Time sheets and vacation:** book several days at once, ad hoc bookings, no overlaps on the same cost 2, vacation booked as time sheets automatically, availability entries, team vacation calendar.
- **Migrated to the new interface:** users, team calendars, addresses and campaigns, leave applications and account, employees, scripts, polls, contracts, banking, visitor book, memos, Merlin templates, my account and more; the former React interface is removed.
- **Notifications and operations:** rules notifying in the app, by mail and SMS, a system dashboard with scheduler and caches, an admin log viewer and an editor for `+projectforge.properties+`; `+config.xml+` is replaced by configuration parameters.
- **Security:** stricter access checks, Content Security Policy, CSRF check for every changing request, POST only for changes, brute force protection for password changes, optional second factor on more pages.
- **Search and usability:** search ignores accents and umlaut spellings, selection boxes without inactive entries and name matches first, a German version of the website.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====
ProjectForge 9.1 sums up all 9.0.x builds since 9.0.0: a file store in the database replacing the JCR, a chat, many pages migrated to the new interface, contribution margins per order and structure element, notifications, a system dashboard and a lot of security hardening.

[red]##**Last release with JCR and Java 17**## - 9.1.x is the last line that runs on Java 17 and supports the JCR (Apache Oak). Releases from 9.2 on have no JCR any more, the files are kept in the database and in the file system. **If you still use the JCR, migrate with 9.1.x first** (`+projectforge.files.store=db+`, check the report), before you update to 9.2 or later. See the admin guide, "Moving the files out of the JCR".

**Before updating** - Back up the database (and the JCR, if you still use it); its schema is migrated automatically at the first start.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- 9.1.x is the last release that runs on Java 17 and supports the JCR (Apache Oak). From 9.2 on there is no JCR any more and Java 21 is required. Installations still using the JCR have to migrate their files with 9.1.x first (admin guide, "Moving the files out of the JCR"); a JCR backup ZIP can't be imported by later releases.

++++
{% include download-link.html %}
++++

[discrete#release-9-0-18.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.0.18 released

[.changelog-source]
__2026-10-27, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.0.18-RELEASE[9.0.18-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.0.18-RELEASE" docker="9.0.18" mini=true %}+++

- **Chat**: confidential conversations, search in all messages, compact bubble layout, unread badge in the top bar
- Liquidity forecast: number of days freely selectable
- Search: closed task structure elements no longer in the menu quick search

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **Chat:** a confidential message in a direct message is now a confidential conversation, end-to-end encrypted and never stored by the server, until one side ends it; the fingerprint covers both keys. Conversations are more compact, with message bubbles, grouped messages and a separator per day.
- **Chat:** the search of the chat page also finds messages in all readable conversations, with a preview of the newest match; a click jumps to the message. A speech bubble in the top bar links to the chat and shows the unread messages, as does the menu entry.
- **Liquidity forecast:** the number of days can be entered freely (1 to 600), the usual horizons remain as quick picks.
- **Search:** closed task structure elements are no longer found in the menu quick search; the detailed search still finds them, struck through.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- Chat: the search of the chat page also finds messages in all readable conversations, each with a preview of the newest match; a click jumps to the message, also in a thread.
- Chat: a speech bubble in the top bar links to the chat, a counter shows the unread messages there and at the menu entry.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- Chat: more compact conversations with message bubbles (own messages on the right), consecutive messages of the same author grouped and a separator per day.
- Liquidity forecast: the number of days can be entered freely (1 to 600), the usual horizons remain as quick picks.
- Search: closed task structure elements are no longer found in the menu quick search. The detailed search still finds them and shows them struck through, as do the structure tree, the paths and the lists.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- Chat: a confidential message in a direct message is now a confidential conversation. Both sides write back and forth, end-to-end encrypted and never stored by the server, until one side ends it. The fingerprint now covers both keys, so a forged message shows as a difference.
====

[discrete#release-9-0-17.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.0.17 released

[.changelog-source]
__2026-10-26, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.0.17-RELEASE[9.0.17-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.0.17-RELEASE" docker="9.0.17" mini=true %}+++

- **Chat in the data transfer**: every area is a chat room, direct messages from personal boxes
- **Avatars** in the chat and the user menu
- Chat: members list, quotes and search
- Project list: Excel export, customer shown in the project selection
- Unreachable mail server no longer slows down saving orders

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **Chat in the data transfer:** every data transfer area is a chat room for everybody with access to it (its admins moderate), files sent in the chat go into the area; external users see only the files. The personal box of another user opens the direct message with them. The buttons Chat and Direct message and the chat page show the unread messages.
- **Chat:** every conversation lists its members with their avatars; messages can quote another message; a search box narrows the direct messages and the rooms; the room page shows the formatted description of the room and is edited there.
- **Avatars:** users upload their own picture under My account, cut square in a new image editor (also used for the images of addresses); it is shown in the chat and in the user menu to all users sharing a group. Administrators can change or remove any avatar.
- **Projects:** Excel export of the project list; the project selection and the project filters show the customer of each project; the first proposed local project number can be set per number range.
- **Notifications:** the bell lists the archived entries of the last 90 days, so a notification confirmed by mistake can still be opened.
- **Usability:** group fields show the members of a group on hover, customer and project groups in list filters show what they comprise; deleted or deactivated users, groups and employees are struck through in more places; users are found by their nickname; a selected structure element is removed with its own (x); in a list with more than 100 entries a button selects the first 100 for a mass update.
- **Fixed:** with the mail server unreachable, saving an order waited once per recipient of its notification and every notification mail waited for the timeout; the gateway serves the subscriptions of team calendars and of the weeks of the year; the project wizard offered no cost 2 types after "Configure another element".
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- Addresses: a small image editor cuts a square out of a chosen image, or the one already shown, before it is uploaded (drag and zoom).
- **Chat in the data transfer**
  * Every data transfer area is a chat room for everybody with access to it (its admins moderate): the button Chat on the area opens it, files sent in the chat go into the area. External users don't see the chat, only the files with their descriptions; the chat of an area with external access says so. Hiding a message doesn't hide its file in the area, deleting the message deletes it.
  * The personal box of another user has the button Direct message, which opens the direct message with them; the files go into their personal box.
  * The chat page lists the chats of the data transfer areas with messages, with unread counts.
  * The buttons Chat and Direct message show the number of unread messages. In a chat, a badge at the top right shows the unread messages not seen yet; a click jumps to the next one, also into a thread.
- Chat: every conversation, also of a data transfer area, lists its members with their avatars (icon at the top right).
- Number ranges: the first proposed local project number can be set per range in the accounting configuration, e.g. 5.###.01 instead of 5.###.00; lower numbers can still be entered.
- Group fields (e.g. the access lists of calendars, address books and polls): hovering a group shows its members, for whoever may see the group.
- Project list: Excel export of the filtered projects with all their fields.
- Avatars: users upload their own picture under My account (cut square in the image editor); it is shown in the chat and in the user menu to all users sharing at least one group. Administrators can change or remove the avatar of any user. A click on the own avatar in the user menu opens it under My account.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- **Chat**
  * The room page shows the description of the room, now formatted text; the creator and the moderators edit the room from there.
  * A search box on the chat page narrows the direct messages and the rooms.
  * Messages can quote another message of the conversation: the quote shows its author and the beginning of its text, a click shows the message.
  * Menu search: the menu entries found come first again, the users found to chat with follow them.
- List filters: customer and project groups show the customers and projects they comprise as tooltip.
- Deleted or deactivated users, groups and employees are now struck through in more places: lists with several names (group members, access lists, contact persons, substitutes), the task tree, chat, history, attachments, the vacation account, booking grants, the HR view, absence charts and the notification log.
- **Mass update**
  * In the selection mode of a list with more than 100 entries, a button selects the first 100 of them, the most a mass update changes at once.
- Notifications: the bell has a button "Archived entries" listing the confirmed or finished notifications of the last 90 days, so a notification confirmed by mistake can still be read and opened.
- Project selection of the edit pages and project filter of the lists and statistics: each project shows its customer in brackets.
- Structure element selection: a selected structure element is removed with its own (x) (not for mandatory fields), the home icon opens the tree.
- User selection: users are also found by their nickname.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- Gateway: subscriptions of team calendars and of the weeks of the year are served, holidays in the language of the user; the token within the subscription url is checked as on the main instance.
- Notifications: if the mail server isn't reachable, a failed notification mail is logged only once with its stack trace and its cause is shown in the delivery state; the further mails of the run wait for the next run instead of each waiting for the timeout.
- Orders: if the mail server can't be reached, saving waits only once for it instead of once per recipient of the notification.
- Project wizard: after "Configure another element" the project step offered no cost 2 types any more, so the next project had to get them in its edit form afterwards.
====

[discrete#release-9-0-16.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.0.16 released

[.changelog-source]
__2026-10-26, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.0.16-RELEASE[9.0.16-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.0.16-RELEASE" docker="9.0.16" mini=true %}+++

- **Chat**: rooms, direct messages, files, threads, mentions and confidential messages
- **Search** ignores accents and umlaut spellings
- Project selection finds projects by number and customer
- Order and invoice caches no longer refresh each other endlessly

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **Chat** (menu Common → Chat): rooms with chosen users and groups, and direct messages to any user, readable by their participants only, administrators neither. Messages with formatting, files of any type (stored in the data transfer), emoji reactions, threads that can be followed and marked unread, and @ mentions notified in the app and by mail. Confidential messages in direct messages are end-to-end encrypted and never stored by the server. Behind a reverse proxy, the chat needs an unbuffered connection, see the administration guide.
- **Search:** search and selection boxes ignore accents and German umlaut spellings ("Mueller" finds "Müller", "Strasse" finds "Straße"), completely after the next nightly re-index; deactivated users are no longer found in the search of the main menu.
- **Administration:** the backup script of the administration guide compresses the dump of the files to about half the size.
- **Fixed:** the order and invoice caches refreshed each other endlessly when an invoice referred to a deleted order position; projects are found by their number and the name of their customer; outgoing invoices saved in the new interface are found by their customer at once; the time sheet filter for sub structure elements can be switched off; postal codes like "D-34286" are no longer linked as JIRA issues; the log of a running script is shown again.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- Chat: confidential messages in direct messages (e.g. for a password), end-to-end encrypted in both browsers, relayed live and never stored by the server, shown to the recipient only once.
- **Chat**
  * Chat rooms (menu Common → Chat): anybody creates a room and chooses its participants, users and groups; members who join a group later take part at once. The creator and the moderators edit and delete the room. Rooms are visible to their participants only, administrators included.
  * Direct messages: anybody can write privately to any user shown in the user selection, from the chat page, from a user found in the menu search (start chat / send file; for everybody, with the users of the user selection) or by clicking an author in any conversation; whoever got a message can answer. Only the two read the conversation, administrators neither.
  * Messages with formatting (text colours, lists, links, inline code and code blocks of several lines), files of any type (paste, drag & drop or file dialog; images as thumbnails), emoji reactions and replies as threads of their own, which can be followed. The files are stored in the data transfer: in an area per room, whose participants see it in the data transfer and where the files are kept as long as chosen in the room; files of direct messages go into the personal box of the recipient. Without the data transfer plugin, no files are exchanged. Own messages can be edited and deleted, moderators hide messages with a reason and see the history of a message.
  * Typing @ suggests the participants of the room; a mentioned person is notified at once, in the app and by mail. New messages are notified once per room until read, by mail only if not seen in the app within an hour; rooms can be muted.
  * New messages appear without reload (server-sent events, with polling as fallback). Behind a reverse proxy, the chat needs an unbuffered connection, see the administration guide.
- Chat: a file of a message can also be opened in its data transfer area, besides downloading it.
- Chat: a message can be marked unread, threads with unread replies are marked, and in a thread a line shows the first unread reply.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- Search and selection boxes ignore accents and German umlaut spellings: "Andre" finds "André", "Mueller" and "Muller" find "Müller", "Strasse" finds "Straße", and vice versa. Applies to entries indexed after the update, i.e. completely after the next nightly re-index.
- Admin guide: the backup script compresses the dump of the files (about half the size), because pg_dump writes their contents hex encoded.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- Outgoing invoices: invoices saved in the new interface were not found by the name of their customer until the next search index rebuild.
- JIRA links: an issue key needs at least two leading uppercase letters, so a postal code like "D-34286" in a text is no longer linked as an issue.
- Project selection: projects are also found by their number (e.g. 7.002) and by the name of their customer.
- Scripts: showing the log of a running script could fail with an error.
- Time sheet list: the filter including all sub structure elements could not be switched off. It is replaced by the filter "without structure sub elements", off by default.
- The order and invoice caches no longer refresh each other endlessly (e.g. during the daily order book snapshots) when an invoice refers to a deleted order position.
- Search in the main menu: deactivated users are no longer found (they still are in the user list).
====

[discrete#release-9-0-15.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.0.15 released

[.changelog-source]
__2026-10-25, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.0.15-RELEASE[9.0.15-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.0.15-RELEASE" docker="9.0.15" mini=true %}+++

- **Ad hoc bookings**: grant or propose time sheet bookings without group membership
- **Notifications**: SMS delivery, creditor invoices due, variables with examples
- Time sheet form: recently used entries with consumption, sortable and filterable
- Customer wizard reuses existing structure elements
- Structure tree: lost and incomplete elements after a background reload fixed
- Password forgotten: reset mail limited against mail bombing

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **Ad hoc bookings:** who may edit the time sheets of others on a structure element grants colleagues the booking of own time sheets for a period, optionally restricted to some cost units; the colleagues see only the granted structure elements. Employees without this right may propose such a booking, the project management accepts the time sheets afterwards (reminded by a new notification rule).
- **Notifications:** delivery steps by SMS; new rule "Creditor invoices due"; the rule editor lists the variables for subject and text with example values and a copy button, the preview shows the texts with example values.
- **Creditor invoices:** marked as overdue already 2 working days before the due date.
- **Time sheet form:** the recently used entries show the consumption of their budget and can be sorted, filtered and arranged per column (remembered per user); the consumption bar tooltip shows budget, booked and remaining person days.
- **Customer wizard:** existing structure elements of the customer and the project can be used instead of new ones, picked from the tree or found by the same title.
- **Order statistics:** the bubble size of the contribution margin chart shows the contribution margin; titles can be switched on.
- **Fixed:** structure elements created or moved during a background reload could vanish from the structure tree, the responsible person was missing after a change; an invalid search syntax shows a hint instead of an empty list; the info of a structure element is only answered to users who may see it; the password reset mail is limited per user, per client and in total, so it can no longer be requested over and over.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- **Ad hoc bookings**
  * Who may edit the time sheets of others on a structure element (e.g. project management, finance) may grant colleagues the booking of own time sheets for a period, without group membership: several colleagues at once, on the structure element and any of its sub elements, each optionally restricted to some of its cost units. The grant is active right away, each colleague gets a mail with the links to book on.
  * The colleagues see only the granted structure elements and the titles of their ancestors in the structure tree: no other structure elements, consumption, time sheets of others or statistics. After the period or a revocation the own time sheets stay readable.
  * In the structure tree, a badge marks the structure elements with ad hoc bookings; its tooltip names the colleagues and their periods. Shown only to who may grant on the structure element.
  * Employees without this right may propose such a booking on the structure elements they book on themselves, for 31 days at most: the colleague books right away, the project management accepts the time sheets afterwards, unchanged or moved to another structure element or cost unit (time sheet form or mass update; list filter "Only to be accepted"). Until then they count like any other time sheet. The project management may confirm a proposal, so later bookings don't have to be accepted anymore.
  * New notification rule "Time sheets to be accepted": reminds the project managers of the time sheets still to be accepted (in the app, and by mail if not acknowledged, as configured in the rule). The structure tree shows their number next to the badge.
- Consumption bar (structure tree, task list, time sheet form): the tooltip shows the budget, the booked and the remaining person days as a calculation, an overbooked budget in red.
- Time sheet form: the recently used entries show the consumption of their budget, and the search also matches it.
- **Creditor invoices**
  * Marked as overdue (red) already 2 working days before the due date, so they are paid in time.
  * New notification rule "Creditor invoices due": reports unpaid creditor invoices due within a configurable number of working days (overdue ones of the last 90 days included) to the recipients of the rule.
- **Notifications**
  * The rule editor lists the variables available for subject and text (general ones and those of the rule type), each with a button to copy it.
  * The variables come with an example value each, so it is visible how e.g. a list of invoices looks; the preview also shows the texts with example values.
- Time sheet form: the table of recently used entries can be sorted and filtered per column, its columns can be reordered, resized, pinned and hidden; the layout is remembered per user.
- Notifications: delivery steps by SMS to the mobile phone number of the recipients (if SMS is configured), with an own SMS text of the rule or otherwise the subject and the link.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="improved" %}
++++
- Customer wizard: existing structure elements of the customer and the project can be used instead of new ones, picked from the tree (the title may differ, e.g. "ACME" for "ACME Inc.") or found automatically by the same title.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="changed" %}
++++
- Order statistics, contribution margin bubble chart: the size of a bubble shows its contribution margin instead of its costs. The switch "Show titles" labels the own bubbles with their short title and contribution margin %; switched off, the names are in the tooltip only.

++++
{% include tag.html tag="fixed" %}
++++
- The info of a structure element (title, path, project, customer, consumption) was answered to every logged-in user; now only to users who may see the structure element.
- Structure tree: a structure element created or moved while the tree was being reloaded in the background could vanish from the tree until the next reload, so no sub-element could be created below it ("Parent structure element is required but not found").
- Structure tree: after a structure element was changed, its responsible person was missing in the tree until the next reload.
- Password forgotten: the reset mail is limited per user, per client and in total, so it can no longer be requested over and over (mail bombing, invalidating a pending reset link).
- Lists: a search term that isn't a valid search syntax (e.g. "Project: Alpha") now shows a hint instead of an empty list without explanation.
====

[discrete#release-9-0-14.changelog-release]
=== ProjectForge 9.0.14 released

[.changelog-source]
__2026-10-23, tag https://github.com/micromata/projectforge/tree/9.0.14-RELEASE[9.0.14-RELEASE]__ +++{% include release-pills.html tag="9.0.14-RELEASE" docker="9.0.14" mini=true %}+++

- **Contribution margin** per order and structure element, bubble chart
- **Former React interface** removed
- **Security**: CSRF check for every session, changing requests as POST only
- Fields with several entries: copy, paste and drag entries
- Import of incoming invoices: currencies and header-only exports corrected

.Overview
[%collapsible]
====
- **Contribution margin:** the order statistics break it down by orders and structure elements (a tree with a monthly chart per row) and show a bubble chart of revenue, contribution margin % and costs per project, project group, customer or customer group, in the colors of the business units.
- **Former React interface removed:** all its pages are part of the new interface, old links (`+/react/...+`) lead there.
- **Security:** the CSRF token is checked for every changing request of a logged-in session; changing requests (filters, templates, search index, logout, cancelling a login) are accepted as POST only; history comments need update access; npm dependencies updated.
- **Fields with several entries:** entries can be selected, copied, cut, pasted and dragged into another field of the same kind; Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes a change.
- **Administration:** structure tree and list show the groups with access rights on an element; the time sheet mass update remaps the cost unit by type, keeping the structure element.
- **Polls:** templates have the state "Template" and no deadline.
- **Fixed:** import of incoming invoices (currencies, periods, header-only exports); cancellation invoices listed with the positions they cancel; the order edit page no longer jumps; the mass update log shows the updated entries again.
====

.All changes
[%collapsible]
====

++++
{% include tag.html tag="added" %}
++++
- Order statistics, contribution margin: bubble chart of revenue, contribution margin % and costs (size) per project, project group, customer or customer group. On request, the other projects of the selection (e.g. of the whole business unit) are shown for comparison, anonymously. The bubbles take the colors of the business units, set with the business units (customer groups page). A switch labels all bubbles with their short title instead (the group name, for a single project its short name).
- Fields with several entries (users, groups, employees, …): entries can be selected by sweeping over them with the mouse or by clicking, then copied (Ctrl/Cmd+C) or cut (Ctrl/Cmd+X) and pasted into another field of the same kind with Ctrl/Cmd+V, or dragged there. Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes a change of the field.
